Nobody should ever think about sync. Edits appear on the other device before you pick it up.

Local first. The interface never waits for the network.

Conflicts resolve silently unless meaning would be lost.

differences: Independent 1920x1080 DOM/CSS/SVG reconstruction; source media is only referenced in external research viewer and is not bundled or copied into the preset.
26-second adaptation expands the 15.6-second source for three readable menu choices and list reflows; cursor, click rings, exact timing and explanatory subtitle wording are original.
Publisher get_bb_app is credited as publisher. Software identity follows the visible CURSOR SIDEBAR title. No full IDE/editor was observed or added.

Ordering, Show, Status filter, Environment filter, Expand All and Mark All as Read remain observed visible menu roots; unobserved outcomes are not implemented.

No real AI task execution or status changes were demonstrated by the grouping sequence.

works.title: 分栏拖动 · 三个吸附点与自由比例
works.author: Gabriell / @gabriell_lab

acceptedSamples.description: Equal article panels, two image areas, middle blue three-dot grip; W374/W374 and blue 50% readout.
Left card narrow and right card wide; left photo cover-crops and body wraps/fades. W187/W561, snapped blue 25%.
Two cards return to equal width; divider and W374/W374 align with blue 50%.
Left card wide and right card narrow, hand at the grip; right content wraps and image crops. W561/W187 and snapped blue 75%.
Equal panels, central grip and blue 50% readout again.
Free ratio with slightly wider left card; W405/W343 and black 54% chip distinguish free position from snapping.
Further free drag toward the right; W485/W263, black 65%, grip between actual card edges.
Final equal split, W374/W374 and blue 50%; same persistent cards and fixed 01/02 footers.

mechanisms: One persistent two-panel reading view; the Sidebar category is a tag, not evidence of a navigation sidebar.
Horizontal divider drag changes left/right widths inversely while both article cards remain visible.
Observed stable sequence: 50% -> 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 50% -> free 54% -> free 65% -> 50%.
Middle cyan three-dot grip tracks the divider; hand indicates drag.
Bottom floating pill reports two W widths and percentage. Snapped 25/50/75 positions use blue; free 54/65 use black.
Fixed-height images cover-crop as width changes. Body text naturally reflows; narrow content fades toward its lower boundary. Fieldnotes label, title and fixed 01/02 footers remain.
differences: 1920x1440 source is adapted to a 1920x1080, 26-second editable composition with longer reading holds; individual drag speeds are authored.
Both source photographs are replaced with independently coded SVG landscape illustrations; no source pixels are included in the preset.

The source's entire parabola article body is replaced with an independently written example of similar length. Short functional labels, title and page numbers remain; text wrapping behavior is preserved.
Width readouts show the actual widescreen card widths (1476px total), rather than copying the source's 748-unit readouts. Percentage, card edges and grip all derive from the same ratio.
Entry animation, click ring, pointer pressure animation, lower proof label and final result caption are original explanatory additions.
No live user drag handler is claimed. The preset is a deterministic GSAP demonstration of observed actions with direct and reverse seeking.
unknowns: The source application, implementation code, actual pointer-event handling and precise snap thresholds are not verified.
The source's reported W unit is not confirmed as physical screen pixels.
Accepted stable frames establish positions and visual states; exact interpolation, duration of each live drag and all intermediate cursor frames were not exhaustively verified.
Source behavior outside this 14.303571-second video is unknown.
works.sourceObservationMethod: Exact source card modal and original href read; original remote video actually paused/viewed at accepted samples. No remote pixels distributed. Not a full original source-code replica or real service execution.
